text:
ana: Heads up — eval dropped on the quantized-m2 bringup for parsing benchmarks. Not huge but consistent across seeds. can someone look at promptset / split artifacts? :thinking_face:

matt: Which run? link please?

ana: run id `2026-03-19-34-quant-m2` (dashboard: <https://redwood.example/runs/2026-03-19-34>). Quick grep from the runner logs shows repeated prompt ids in both train/test: `grep -n "prompt_id" artifacts/2026-03-19-34/* | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head` ->

```
> 23 artifacts/2026-03-19-34/test_prompts.json: prompt_id=Qp_3821
> 23 artifacts/2026-03-19-34/train_prompts.json: prompt_id=Qp_3821
> 12 artifacts/.../test_prompts.json: prompt_id=Qp_4400
```

ana: That looked wrong so I ran `jq '.[] | .id' ...` and got identical ids. Not sure if synthetic generator bug or CI fixture reuse.

matt: Interesting. I saw a flaky test a while back where the synthetic generator used a global `RNG_SEED` env var. Could CI layer caching be reusing the fixture across split jobs?

liya: digging — the synthetic generator in `eval-fixtures/gen.py` uses `seed = os.environ.get('CI_FIXTURE_SEED') or int(time.time())` and then calls `random.seed(seed)` early, but the runner later does `random.seed(seed)` again with the same value when regenerating different splits. The problem is the CI job sets `CI_FIXTURE_SEED` in global env during the `prepare-fixtures` step and then caches the generated artifact. So train/test jobs both pick up the cached fixture instead of regenerating with independent seeds.

sam: right — our CI uses image layer caching for `/workspace/fixtures` so `make ci-fixtures` writes to `./fixtures/cache.tar` and subsequent split jobs untar that. If the generator wasn't parameterized by split name, the cache will be identical across splits.

eval-bot: automated check: 23 duplicated prompt ids found between train/test for promptset `parsing-v2.1`. Overlap percentage: 0.6%. Flagging as dataset leakage.

ana: ok — quick mitigation: change fixture generator to derive seed like `seed = hash(commit_sha + split_name) % (2**32)` so different splits always get a different seed even if CI cache is hit. I'll open a small PR.

matt: good. also add a post-generation check in the eval runner: assert `len(set(train_ids) & set(test_ids)) == 0`, fail CI if overlap > 0 and require manual approval. That will catch cached-object issues earlier.

liya: agreed. also we should bump promptset version when fixtures are regenerated; otherwise downstream dashboards will be confusing. Add `promptset_version` metadata to the tarball.

sam: PR link?

ana: opened: <https://redwood.example/pulls/2892> — patch modifies `gen.py` + adds `--split-name` flag, changes seed derivation, and adds a smoke check script `check_no_overlap.py`.

ci-bot: @matt triggered re-run of `eval-ci/parsing-v2.1` (job 9845) — started at 1812350150.

eval-bot: rerun result: fixtures regenerated with new seed logic, overlap check passed (0 duplicates). New run `2026-03-19-34-quant-m2-retry` shows metrics back in baseline range.

ana: great — will merge after one approval. After merge, we should: regenerate all fixtures, bump promptset to `parsing-v2.2`, and push a short note in the release changelog about the fix.

matt: add to the release checklist and notify support so customers on dedicated/private don't see weird eval diffs during the roll. :+1:

liya: I'll add an integration test to CI that intentionally caches `fixtures/cache.tar` and ensures `--split-name` changes outputs. quick unit added in PR.

sam: thanks everyone. follow-ups: (1) regen artifacts and upload to S3, (2) tag promptset v2.2, (3) run full eval-harness smoke for quantized-m2.

ana: noted. I'll coordinate the regen and S3 upload tomorrow morning (UTC). :calendar:
